chapter: Compositions, singers and the end of the big band
title: Jimmy Mitchelle, Ida James and Delores Brown
summary: Mitchelle became the main vocalist; Ida James and Delores Brown sang with the band.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Now, Jimmy Mitchelle. You said you didn't realize he was a singer until a particular point.

Well. he asked me to let him sing and I'm, sing a tune the last year we was in school. You know, the last year we was in school. And then, I started adding vocals in there in a different arrangement. You know, one that he liked, that he could sing. But, he started, and he started building himself up. My mother-in-law, she likes Jimmy Mitchelle's voice. This was the time before you started getting all the other singers out. She looked for Jimmy Mitchelle's vocal like "Song of the Wanderer," "Cherry", "Somebody's Rocking My Dream Boat", I think that Jimmy did on recordings, and quite a few others there which you know cause he did most of the singing. "Don't Cry Baby". That was a big one.
Right. And, who else functioned as either a male or a female singer in your band that we haven't mentioned so far?

Dolly Lyons. She is one of the girls. Effie Smith. I got her in California. Oh, Ida James. She was the first girl vocalist I had. She, all those years with Earl Hines - for a short time - (inaudible) Then she was with me about, maybe about 8 years.

DeLores Brown. She did quite a few recordings for me. I got DeLores Brown, she was singing along with Duke along with Ivie Anderson. Duke had two vocalists. They were at Loew's State and I went down to catch Duke. And, I saw them both. I went backstage, this is after hours. I said Duke, you don't need two vocalists. I said I like DeLores there. He said go talk to her if you want her.
And she was with me for quite awhile and she married Marsalis Green, the trumpet player with me then.
